title: CLO 2025.1 - Added Zipper to Object Window
description: CLO 2025.1 new version fully upgraded, further enhancing your work efficiency! The new version's object window adds a zipper tab option, allowing zippers of the same style to be managed as a single item, enabling a faster and more efficient workflow.
transcript:
This video is to introduce the relevant update of the chain.  
In the previous version, when you needed to change the attribute of a 3D or more complex chain on a piece of clothing,  
you had to select each chain one by one and modify them individually.  
In the 2025.1 version, the object window has added a new chain selection tab.  
You can manage chains according to samples, and save and apply them to the entire chain.  
First of all, when you look at the object window, a new chain selection tab is added here.  
From the current version onward, operations related to the chain will be controlled through this selection tab.  
Press the plus button in the upper right corner to create a new default chain pattern.  
Then apply the newly created chain to the clothing.  
First, select the 3D chain to be applied in the 3D window.  
Then press the apply button on the right side of the new chain in the object window.  
You can apply it this way.  
If you first select a chain, then click the apply button in the upper right corner of the object window,  
a new default chain will be created at the bottom and applied directly to the selected 3D chain.  
The copy function duplicates a similar chain pattern.  
Select a chain in the object window.  
In the attribute editor at the bottom,  
you can modify the overall shape of the chain,  
including the basic information of the chain, the chain type, and the chain size.  
You can see the changes reflected.  
The corresponding chain in the 3D window will also change.  
While maintaining the overall shape,  
you can also select and edit details of various components such as the editor, the head, and the chain links.  
When you use the option to press and hold the head, the chain, or the stop component,  
it will immediately select the entire chain component.  
At this time, if you press and hold the button again to edit the object,  
it will select only a specific object.  
If the selected object is divided into two or more grids,  
press and hold the button again to select only a specific object.  
Here, click the chain part again to edit the size of the chain separately.  
After modification, the chain component will be selected again.  
You can press and hold the button again to edit the material color of a specific part separately.  
You can also unify the modifications.  
You can also select both the chain and the cloth to modify the material color, etc.  
This is the same as in the previous operation.  
You can also save the designed chain pattern in GPS format,  
and use it in other projects.  
In the object window, select the chain to be saved.  
Click the save button at the top of the property editor to save the file.  
The saved ZPS chain file can be opened anytime using the button next to it,  
and reloaded into other projects.  
Here, open another clothing project file.  
In the object window, select the chain,  
find the open icon in the property editor,  
and select the saved ZPS file.  
You can see the new sample in the chain selection tab list,  
and it is also applied to the 3D clothing chain.  
In addition,  
you can press and hold the right mouse button on an unused chain in the object window,  
and you can rename, delete, or reset it.  
This is an effective way to clean up the list by deleting all unused chains.  
You can see the new sample in the object window,  
and it is also applied to the 3D clothing chain.

chunks.content: ## Introduction to Chain Management in CLO 2025.1 This section explains the new chain management features introduced in CLO 2025.1, focusing on the addition of the chain selection tab in the object window. It describes how the update simplifies modifying complex 3D chains on garments by enabling sample-based management and bulk application. In previous versions, changing attributes of a 3D chain required selecting and modifying each chain individually. CLO 2025.1 addresses this by adding a dedicated chain selection tab in the object window, centralizing all chain-related operations. This tab allows users to create, save, and apply chain patterns efficiently across entire garments. --- ## Using the Chain Selection Tab This section details how to create, apply, and duplicate chain patterns using the new chain selection tab and associated controls in the object window. - The chain selection tab is located in the object window and controls all chain operations from this version onward. - To create a new default chain pattern, press the plus (+) button in the upper right corner of the tab. - To apply a chain pattern to a garment: - Select the 3D chain in the 3D window. - In the chain selection tab, press the apply button next to the desired chain pattern. - Alternatively, selecting a 3D chain first and then clicking the apply button in the top right of the object window will create a new default chain at the bottom of the list and apply it directly. - The copy function duplicates an existing chain pattern for easy modification. --- ## Editing Chain Attributes and Components This section covers modifying chain attributes, including chain type, size, shape, and individual components, using the attribute editor and selection controls. - Select a chain in the object window to display its attributes in the property editor. - Modify overall chain properties such as chain type, size, and shape, with changes immediately reflected in the 3D window. - For detailed editing, components like the head, chain links, and stopper can be selected and modified individually. - Holding the selection button while clicking a component selects the entire chain component. - Pressing and holding the selection button again toggles between selecting the entire component or individual objects within it. - If an object is subdivided into multiple grids, repeated presses allow selection down to specific sub-objects. - Chain link size can be edited separately by selecting the chain part again. - Material colors of specific parts can be edited individually or unified across chain and cloth components. - Material editing applies the same way as in previous versions, allowing simultaneous modification of chain and garment materials. --- ## Saving and Reusing Chain Patterns This section describes how to save customized chain patterns in the ZPS format and reuse them across different projects. - In the object window, select the chain pattern to save. - Click the save button at the top of the property editor to export the chain pattern as a ZPS file.

chunks.content: - Material editing applies the same way as in previous versions, allowing simultaneous modification of chain and garment materials. --- ## Saving and Reusing Chain Patterns This section describes how to save customized chain patterns in the ZPS format and reuse them across different projects. - In the object window, select the chain pattern to save. - Click the save button at the top of the property editor to export the chain pattern as a ZPS file. - Saved ZPS files can be loaded anytime using the open button next to the save control. - To reuse a saved chain pattern: - Open another clothing project. - Select the chain in the object window. - Use the open icon in the property editor to import the saved ZPS file. - The imported chain pattern appears in the chain selection tab and is applied to the 3D clothing chain. --- ## Managing Chain Samples: Rename, Delete, and Reset This section explains how to manage chain samples within the object window, including renaming, deleting, and resetting unused chains to maintain an organized workspace. - Right-click on an unused chain sample in the object window to access options to rename, delete, or reset it. - Deleting unused chains helps clean up the list and improve workflow efficiency. - Renamed or reset chains update immediately in the chain selection tab and reflect on the 3D garment chain. --- ## Summary CLO 2025.1 introduces a powerful chain selection tab in the object window that streamlines chain pattern creation, editing, application, and management. The update allows batch operations on complex 3D chains, detailed component editing, and convenient saving/loading of chain patterns in ZPS format. Effective sample management tools help maintain a clean project environment while ensuring seamless integration with 3D garment chains.
